image: A battle-worn halberd standing point-up, its long blade whittled down with two deep notches near the top and a single barbed hook jutting off the right edge — a spear shaved to a stub.
A low grassy knoll with two rounded humps rising side by side from a flat baseline of packed earth, the only rise on an otherwise empty plain.
Two forearms interlocked into a cradle, boosting an unseen climber up over a flat stone ledge — the grip that hauls someone straight out of a pit.
A single bamboo skewer driven straight down through two square chunks of grilled chicken, one stacked above the other, still dripping over the coals.
Two short horn stubs poking up and splaying apart from a young goat's brow, each no bigger than a thumb.
A single tall reed bent hard to the left in a gust, its stem sweeping down in one long clean curve to the ground.
A black iron pothook hanging over a hearth: two flat crossbars near the top and a long shaft below that curls into a J to catch a kettle.
A lazy curl of chimney smoke corkscrewing upward from a little tail and flattening into two thin layers of haze at the top.
A lanky festival performer balanced high on two long wooden stilts spread wide apart, a flat little cap perched squarely on top of his head.
A horizontal launch-bar throwing off a shower of four bright sparks that scatter down and outward beneath it, like the first burst of a firework.
A tiny roadside teahouse kiosk: a peaked roof on top, a square serving window in the middle, a jutting eave below it, all balanced on one central support post with a hooked footing.
A half-carved wooden skiff with a sharply peaked prow, curls of wood-shaving heaped around its planked hull and a whittling knife jammed upright into its right flank.
A floppy wide-brimmed hat yanked down low over a face, a single wide unblinking eye glaring out from the shadow beneath its brim.
An open-topped square pit with two sharpened stakes crossed in an X across its floor, waiting for one careless foot to drop in.
A wooden pillory of two upright posts joined by twin crossbars, a heavy execution blade propped and gleaming at its right edge.
A curved bronze breastplate hugging the torso, an X-shaped crack splitting the metal squarely over the heart.
A small square lacquered wooden sake cup, its rim heaped with rice and struck perfectly flat by a flick of a bamboo stick.
A slanting cliff-ledge overhanging two neat rows of rice stalks that stand side by side beneath it, tallied like a calendar of harvests.
A bent old man thrusting a smoking torch into a boxed-up cupboard, one gnarled hand gripping the brand as he rummages the dark inside.
A shepherd's-crook hook curling down to cradle a small open mouth, snatching a spoken word clean out of the air.
A boxy roadside kiosk under a hooked overhanging roof, a stern mouth set in its service window barking orders at the queue outside.
An upright stone fountain-statue standing stiffly at attention, its pursed mouth jetting a hard stream of water straight outward, spitting back whatever gets poured into it.
A towering multi-tiered pagoda that soars skyward yet tilts at its slanted, peaked top, a single dark doorway gaping open at its base.
A bare tree whose upper branches hold three wide-open bird-beaks crowded together, the whole crown ringing with a shrill, noisy chorus of chirping.
A weeping willow whose long fronds hang straight down in drooping symmetrical pairs over a low earthen mound, every branch sagging heavily toward the ground.
A broad, barrel-chested strongman in his robust prime, muscles bulging as he stands squarely beside a tall split bed-plank propped up at his left shoulder.
A figure curled on its side asleep beneath a low crescent moon, knees tucked up and spine bent into a comma, reclining for the night.
A broad-shouldered figure striding along with a small stowaway pinned tight under each armpit, both arms clamped down so neither little captive can wriggle free.
A worshipper lifting a bound sheaf of wheat high in both upturned hands, three cord-bindings crossing its upright stalk, presenting it as a reverent offering.
A lighthouse keeper hoisting a blazing lantern overhead in both arms, its broad hood-housing cresting above his wide-planted stance, flooding the whole scene with brilliant white light.
A figure gripping a knife to slash three deep notches into a flat wooden tally-stick, sealing a binding vow that will be split so each party keeps one half.
A farmer's hand (寸, thumb cocked to one side) sweeps across a gridded seed-plot (甫), flinging a wide fan of grain that scatters and spreads out over the whole bed.
A peaked temple gable whose ridge flares up into two little ornamental horns, with a square latticed window set in the wall just beneath the eave and a wisp of smoke curling out through it.
A tall pyre of stacked brushwood blazing on a hilltop, a burst of bright sparks scattering out from its base like a spray of tiny dots flung into the dark.
A stick-figure man standing arms-out, one leg dropping straight down while the other kinks sharply sideways at the knee, so he tilts and hobbles on the lame, bent limb.
A robed nun bowed forward under a broad drooping hood that leans out over her, a smaller figure kneeling tucked in close at her feet.
A figure jackknifed almost double, crawling out from beneath a heavy stone overhang that presses down on its spine and forces the whole body into a tight, cramped hunch.
A single young shoot pushing straight up out of bare dirt, its tip splitting into a small Y-fork of first leaves, with one thin root threading down to anchor it.
A green shoot doubled over into a tight hook, straining upward but pinned flat under a heavy slab of packed sod that caps it against a hard ground-line.
A clawed hand grips a carving blade up top, sending curls of fresh wood-shavings and beads of sap raining straight down beneath it to pool below.
A stiff banner-pole with a broad crossbar driven straight down into the center of a plump beating heart, its little pennant marking exactly where the heart is set on going.
Two upturned hands clamped together around the shaft of a dagger-axe, thrusting it up and outward to bar the way — a sentry's braced warning to halt.

A flat wooden shop-sign of thin horizontal slats, its top edge a single hinged door-panel, swinging above an entrance so flat it casts almost no shadow — the door leaf riding over the stacked tablet-slats.
A single blazing sun hovering directly over a double file of ants marching rightward in lock-step — the round 'sun' block riding atop the two paired 'compare' figures below.
A slender millet plant shaped like a little tree, a single glistening bead of sticky sap clinging to the upper-right of its top branch — the tree with one clinging dot.
A curved clan-dagger driven point-down through a stone floor, one bead of its blade pressed flush against a bedrock line drawn beneath it — pinned as low to the ground as a blade can go.
A coil of jet-black silk thread dangling from a small pin-cap, twisting downward into shadow so its lowest loops vanish from sight — fine thread hung beneath a tiny lid.
Two S-curved terracotta tiles hooked into one another, a small nub jutting up like a fixing-peg, both still warm from the kiln — the interlocking pictograph of a tiled roof.
A crooner belting the very last note, the boxy 'sound' block forming his torso and head, balanced on two long striding legs as he steps to the stage edge for the final bow — the finish, after all.

A flat wooden zither — its craftsman's-square frame and a rounded sound-box — laid out beneath a raised split-bamboo beater poised to strike the strings, the bamboo radical arching over the instrument.
A loose fold of moon-pale flesh drooping from a wrinkled old man's jaw like a rooster's wattle — the boxy 'old' block set beside the sagging 'flesh-moon' on the right.
A broad hand clamping down over the barred, upright grid of a bowing minister's eye, gripping so hard the bars bow inward and the knuckles whiten — a firm, unbreakable grasp.
A tiny roadside inn: a sharp peaked roof sheltering a single upright post and a small square doorway below, lamplight glowing through the door for the traveller stopping to lodge for the night.
A squat clay pot with a peaked lid and a round mouth-opening on its front, a tuft of grass sprouting up through the seam of the lid — the little pot of beans that caps the glyph.
A tiger's striped forehead and pricked ears worn as a hood, its dark bars and one hooked whisker-mark hanging like a canopy over whatever crouches beneath it.
A long razor clam propped against a cliff-ledge, its pale muscular foot thrust out below the shell like a farmer's digging blade, quivering as if about to shake the ground.
A downturned hand, fingers splayed into a claw, reaching into the crown of a small tree to pluck a single ripe berry from the branches below it.
A clenched fist seizing the long trailing tail of a bolting animal, loose hairs spraying downward in four wet strands — caught just before it can escape.
A sharp-eyed hunting falcon gripping a single straight crossbar with its talons, wings folded tight against its short-tailed body, one flat bar laid across the top.
A big round head tipped hard to one side, its cheek resting against a small upturned spoon, nodding off for just a little while.
A low open-fronted shed whose slanted roof shelters two tall hemp stalks hung side by side to dry, loose fibres dangling, ready to be ground into a numbing powder.
Two cupped hands pressing a sticky rice ball round and tight above a crossed pair of forearms — the rolling gesture that caps the scroll, ticket, and victory kanji.
Three taut ropes yanked hard in the same direction by unseen hands, all straining together as one — pure combined muscle.
A folded paper fortune-slip tied to a shrine branch, a big lucky 'GOOD' brushed across its top over a little box of tiny print below.
A flat wooden rack studded with a row of short upward teeth along its top edge, sitting on a solid base — the jagged crown of an industrial gear-rack.
A hunched figure on one knee, one arm stretched up with an open palm and the other tucked under a bent back, pleading for a coin.
A single tall stake driven straight down through three stacked horizontal slats, pinning them into one rigid tiered fence-post, lush vines threaded along each rung.
